measurement.note: current composition, taken after the dense_wide256 layer-scope promotion to layers 16-47; the raw CSV holds two prefill passes, all figures here are 1x

geometry.grid_column_semantics: rocprofv3 Grid_Size_X/Y report total work-items (grid_dim * workgroup_size), not grid dimensions; 163840 = 1280*128 and 256 = 256*1

roofline.verdict: weight-bandwidth-bound at 59% of DRAM peak. 90.3% of the traffic is a 256x re-read of the same 3.48 MB weight tensor, because the dequantized weight is reused across only ROW_BATCH=4 rows.

weight_reread_mechanism.why: row_base = blockIdx.y * ROW_BATCH and blockIdx.y spans rows/ROW_BATCH = 256. Every row-batch sweeps all 1280 hidden tiles, so the whole 3.48 MB weight tensor is swept once per row-batch. The reuse distance is the full 3.48 MB, which is served from DRAM, not cache.
weight_reread_mechanism.access_pattern_is_not_the_problem: q8_0_weight_wave_scale (gguf_k_gemv.hip:105) uses __builtin_amdgcn_readfirstlane for the block index, so all 32 lanes of a warp read one 34-byte q8_0 block: the 2-byte scale is broadcast and the 32 quant bytes are lane-indexed (k & 31 == lane). The read is coalesced, not a gather.
weight_reread_mechanism.basis_correction: docs/REFACTOR.md 'GR-Up Wide Tile' states the fused kernel's weight traffic as 3.565 GB and 1.88 FLOP/byte. That is the f32-DEQUANTIZED size (10240*320*4 = 13.11 MB, x256 = 3.355 GB), not the packed q8_0 tensor the kernel actually reads (3.48 MB, x256 = 891 MB). The real operational intensity on weight traffic is 7.53 FLOP/byte, 4x the recorded figure. The conclusion 'the limiter is weight traffic' survives - 90% of traffic is still the re-read - but the magnitude does not. The wide tile's recorded 13.9 MB / 483 FLOP/byte has the same conflation: 13.9 MB is its f16 LDS staging size, while its DRAM weight read is the same 3.48 MB packed tensor.

epilogue_estimate.method: instruction count from source, not a counter measurement
epilogue_estimate.store_coalescing_risk: gate[index] with index = row*10240 + branch*2560 + hidden_base + col. Per block the 8 active threads write 2 consecutive floats (col 0,1) per (row, branch): 4 branches at 10 KB stride and 4 rows at 40 KB stride, so 32 scattered 4-byte stores covering up to 32 cache lines. The 64-byte line at hidden_base is shared with the 7 neighbouring blocks at consecutive blockIdx.x, so merging depends on their co-residency and is not established here.
epilogue_estimate.note: This is the one component the trace cannot separate; the projection/epilogue split needs a variant microbenchmark at the same geometry, not a counter reading.

levers.why: halves the weight re-read, 891 MB -> 445 MB per launch, taking total traffic to 541 MB and the operational intensity from 6.8 to 12.4 FLOP/byte. The per-output k-order, the 16/8/4/2/1 shuffle tree, and the 4-wave LDS sum are all untouched: ROW_BATCH only adds independent row accumulators, and weights[branch][col] is dequantized once and consumed by all rows in the same order.
levers.cost: acc[8][4][2] is 64 floats against 32 at RB4, plus weight_rows[4][2] pointers; estimated 66 -> 98 VGPRs, so about 7 -> 5 blocks/CU.
levers.existing_evidence_does_not_test_this: The 2026-09-06 RB8/HT1 retile halved the re-read and measured 0.80x. It changed ROW_BATCH and HIDDEN_TILE together: HT1 halves the FMAs per x load and doubles the block count, so it is a confounded experiment, not evidence about row batching. Only a rowbatch4 kernel exists in-tree (gguf_k_gemv.hip:952); no clean RB8/HT2 variant has ever been built here.
levers.estimated_prize_basis: traffic reduction of 350 MB per launch at the measured 151 GB/s effective rate; an upper bound that assumes the kernel stays bandwidth-bound and occupancy loss is free

levers.why: In the fused_up path the kernel writes gate[index] and then uses its own local sigmoid_gate to build mixed. Nothing reads scratch.gate afterwards: the follow-up qwen4_exp_sigmoid_f32 is guarded by `not fused_up and not fused_sigmoid_mean` (qwen4_exp_runner.py:3127) and is skipped. The 41.9 MB/launch store is dead.
levers.cost: a separate kernel entry point without the store, or a template parameter
levers.estimated_prize_basis: 41.9 MB/launch at 151 GB/s, 4.3% of the kernel; does not include the store-coalescing amplification, which would only increase it
levers.verify_before_implementing: the dead-store claim holds for the fused_up path only. The gr_wide and gr_iu8 paths DO read scratch.gate back (their separate sigmoid and gated_mean kernels), so a template parameter is safer than deleting the store outright.

levers.why: doubles the FMAs per x load (32 -> 64 per xv) and halves the block count and epilogue invocations. It does not change weight traffic, because the re-read factor is rows/ROW_BATCH and is independent of the hidden tiling.
levers.cost: acc[4][4][4] is 64 floats and weight_rows[4][4] is 16 pointers; same register class as lever 1, so the two cannot be combined for free
levers.estimated_prize_basis: instruction-efficiency only; the kernel is at 3.4% of FP32 peak, so this addresses a non-binding resource

levers.lever: fuse the grouped-rmsnorm producer of normalized
levers.arithmetic: preserving if the rmsnorm arithmetic is unchanged
levers.why: normalized is read for 41.9 MB/launch. If a separate kernel produces it, fusing removes that launch plus its write and this read.
levers.cost: needs the producer identified; not established in this pass

levers.why: Recorded in the task's no-arithmetic-risk trio, but the source does not support it as an independent lever: at ROW_BATCH=4 x BRANCHES=4 x HIDDEN_TILE=2 there are already 32 independent FMA chains per thread. ILP is not the limiter; traffic is, and lever 1 is the traffic lever.

arithmetic_change_is_closed.finding: The GR family is closed to arithmetic change for an independent reason, recorded in docs/REFACTOR.md. Every measured arithmetic route saturates the production gate at 1.3e-3 - 1.6e-3 mean KL, including corrections more accurate than the incumbent.
arithmetic_change_is_closed.shared_mechanism: The MoE router's top-k expert selection is a discrete amplification node: a ~1 ulp router-logit difference flips which of 512 experts runs, which moves the model logits by O(1). Measured on the router warp-reduce candidate at benchmarks/results/2026-09-27-router-warp-reduce/, where all six top-1 mismatches were flip-eligible and none were outside. Every downstream GR or dense arithmetic route inherits that saturation.
arithmetic_change_is_closed.consequence: Levers 1-3 are bit-exact and do not need the numerical gate; they need only the strict parity contract, which they satisfy by construction. This is why they are the only ones ranked as actionable.
